verdict_reason: No compile error found in e76bfe0f and no existing test expected to fail. F1 and F2 are session-crate edits of a few lines; made after the bundled run they would force another session and dependents run, so make them before it. F3 and F4 are lead decisions and do not hold the build.

findings.what: The option A guard treats a cancel as stale records. `validate_multicam_records(&records, document, budget, cancel).is_err()` returns Ok(()) on Code::Canceled, so the guard passes without checking the successor. Nothing after it in submit_inner checks the token before publish (session.rs:1417 routing_takeovers parses only when a sequence is added; session.rs:1480 publishes).
findings.scenario: A timeline step removes a video track of a declared source and the host's cancel lands after the proposal and before or during this first validate (folio tick checks the token on every record). The step commits, Applied.cancel_too_late is true, the valid records are now invalid, and the whole multicam set refuses on read: the state option A forbids. keep_entry_valid at session.rs:1858 handles this correctly. The lane widened this call from Remove-only to every sequence-changing commit.
findings.smallest_fix: Match as keep_entry_valid does: Ok(()) continue; Err(d) if d.code == Code::Canceled => return Err(SessionError::Canceled); Err(_) => return Ok(()). A direct in-crate test with a canceled token is about 6 lines.

findings.what: The model-facing manual still says 'multicam angle_order still goes invalid when its track is removed, read by index'. This lane refuses that commit folio_rejected on every path (tests/routing_repair.rs no_commit_path_changes_the_video_tracks_of_a_declared_source). The same edit updated the string nearby and left this clause.
findings.scenario: A no-context model reading --descriptor expects a commit that goes unreadable and gets a refusal.
findings.smallest_fix: Replace the clause with: a commit that would make a valid multicam record set invalid is refused folio_rejected; a file already stale refuses the whole set on read.

findings.what: The inert rule also removed the refusal on a NEW authored target. MixerEdit::Output and MixerEdit::AddSend rely on validate_audio_routing to refuse a bad bus. A well-formed STRK id the sequence does not hold now returns Ok and adds one undo step, and the audio plays to the master or the send does nothing.
findings.scenario: v.mixer_edit(MixerEdit::AddSend { track_id, target: <typo or stale STRK id>, level: 1.0, pre_fader: false }) is Ok. Before this lane it was an error. The UI offers only held buses (mixer.rs:706, :731), so the reach is programmatic callers and parallel model paths. No existing test pins it (harness tests/audio_mixer.rs:188 uses a held audio track, still refused).
findings.smallest_fix: Lead decision, mixer.rs is outside the lane's owned paths: in mixer_edit_inner, refuse Output and AddSend when the target is not a track of the sequence (about 3 lines). Reading and sequence commits stay inert as ruled. set_audio_routing stays as is: viewer_inert_routing.rs pins that the Viewer's own write is not refused.

findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/harness.rs:1890 (history_step commits the sequence inverse, then swaps the entry) with crates/hsk-studio-session/src/session.rs:1396
findings.what: An undo the guard makes permanently refused. It is the same sequence-before-entry order the lead cited for not refusing a bus removal at commit, so that reason also applies to this ruling; it holds today only because no production caller passes the multicam token.
findings.scenario: Live records R1 do not declare seq-a. run.submit_sequence_and_entry(op, seq-a plus video track V3, "multicam", R2 declaring seq-a with V3) commits: the guard passes on R1, then R2 validates. Undo: the timeline inverse removes V3 while R2 is live and valid, the guard answers folio_rejected, restore puts the step back, and every undo attempt refuses, blocking all history under it. At base this undo worked. git grep: the Viewer passes only ROUTING_ENTRY to these calls; only viewer_mint_skips_inert.rs passes multicam.
findings.smallest_fix: No edit needed for this build. Name it next to undo_corner in the lane notes. If a host ever carries the multicam token, either refuse that token in sequence_and_entry_step, or swap the entry first on undo.

builder_questions.1_undo_by_value: Not wrong for a real undo in one session. Remove inverses carry the live value (multicam_step.rs:165) and every removal passes publish (session.rs:1480, reconcile at :2146), so the digest matches. A real undo reports a takeover only past 128 removals (named), or if a host quoted expect with -0.0 against a live 0.0 (PartialEq equal, JSON digest differs; report only). A real takeover can be missed in two ways: the identical value re-inserted (named), and a set unreadable against the LIVE document that the same step repairs while inserting the sequence (sequence_records.rs:225-228 parses against current only). The second needs a stale file plus a step doing both; report only; not listed as a finding.
builder_questions.2_guard_blocks: No Viewer path is blocked: no Viewer command changes a video track of a sequence or the source of a moded clip outside the multicam step, and razor, trim, move, mute, rename and removing a moded clip all pass (a_step_that_leaves_the_declared_video_tracks_alone_commits_and_undoes). Harness undo is LIFO, so an entry-only step between steps is undone first. The exception is F4, plus the named undo_corner.
builder_questions.3_guard_cost: One call per commit that changes sequences (session.rs:1396), one at resync. Not per clip, not in a planner loop: Viewer razor and nest plan first and commit once. The most frequent caller is a mixer fader drag (mixer.rs:672, Slider changed -> MixerEdit::Volume -> submit_sequence), one commit per changed frame, already a commit, and only on a file with a parseable multicam entry. ReservedIds::of parses once per razor, move, nest, subsequence or source edit, not per mint. The validator is linear (owners BTreeMap, folio multicam.rs:263).
builder_questions.4_takeover_not_surfaced: Confirmed: git grep finds no routing_takeovers in harness-core, harness-view or harness. The Run op record omits it, so at the harness boundary a takeover through Run::submit_sequence_edits is still silent. Viewer mints no longer reach it. It is correct to keep this as a candidate for the host surface; F-R57-3 is closed at the Session API only.
builder_questions.5_wrong_kind: Confirmed as listed and pinned. Not reachable from a Viewer mint: ReservedIds covers every id-bearing field of StudioAudioRouting (routes, output, sends, bus_effects, track_automation, clip_gains, clip_pans). Reach is a direct commit or a file.
builder_questions.test_an_entry_that_does_not_parse_reserv: Asserts its words only as a control. Damaged bytes name no id, so razor_clip(1) is minted with or without the fix, and the test passes on the code before e76bfe0f once the fixture opens. It goes red only if ReservedIds::of or the commit refuses or panics on a damaged entry. Expected green at the tip: the guard's parse fails to Ok, and open_multitrack does not read multicam.
builder_questions.test_harness_path: Asserts what it claims. Without the guard, submit_sequence_and_entry would commit the track removal and then accept the rewritten records, so the first assert goes red. The second assert (submit_sequence_edits_and_entry) is refused by multicam_step validating the live records, which held at base too, so it pins existing behaviour. The sequence and entry byte asserts are real.
